C1.statement: CircuitBreaker guards its mutable state with a sync.Mutex.

C2.statement: Execute obtains a generation and error from beforeRequest before running the request.

C3.statement: If beforeRequest returns an error, Execute returns nil and that error immediately without running the request.

C4.statement: Execute defers a recover handler around the request.

C5.statement: On panic Execute calls afterRequest with success false before re-panicking.

C6.statement: After a normal request, Execute records the outcome via afterRequest using isSuccessful(err).

C7.statement: beforeRequest rejects requests in StateOpen with ErrOpenState.

C8.statement: beforeRequest rejects half-open requests when counts.Requests is at or above maxRequests with ErrTooManyRequests.

C9.statement: Accepted requests increment counts.Requests in beforeRequest.

C10.statement: afterRequest returns without accounting if the generation differs from the one captured before the request.

C11.statement: afterRequest recomputes the current state via currentState before accounting.

C12.statement: In closed state, a success increments totals and resets consecutive failures via counts.onSuccess.

C13.statement: In half-open state, a success closes the breaker when consecutive successes reach maxRequests.

C14.statement: In closed state, a failure calls readyToTrip and opens the breaker if it returns true.

C15.statement: In half-open state, any failure transitions the breaker to open.

C16.statement: In closed state, currentState starts a new generation when expiry is set and has passed.

C17.statement: In open state, currentState transitions to half-open when expiry has passed.

C18.statement: setState is a no-op if the requested state equals the current state.

C19.statement: setState moves to a new generation before invoking onStateChange.

C20.statement: setState invokes onStateChange only if a callback is set, passing name, previous and new state.

C21.statement: toNewGeneration increments the generation and clears counts.

C22.statement: In closed state with interval zero, toNewGeneration leaves expiry at the zero time.

C23.statement: In open state, toNewGeneration sets expiry to now plus timeout.

C24.statement: In half-open state, toNewGeneration leaves expiry at the zero time.

C25.statement: TwoStepCircuitBreaker.Allow returns an error and no callback when beforeRequest fails.

C26.statement: The Allow callback reports the outcome via afterRequest with the captured generation.

C27.statement: Settings docs state ReadyToTrip is called with a copy of Counts whenever a request fails in the closed state.
C27.fragment: ReadyToTrip is called with a copy of Counts whenever a request fails in the closed state.

C28.statement: Execute calls beforeRequest, then on a normal path runs the request and then calls afterRequest.

C29.statement: On panic, Execute calls afterRequest false and then re-panics with the same value.

C30.statement: afterRequest takes the mutex, recomputes state/generation, and returns early when generations differ.

C31.statement: beforeRequest takes the mutex and computes the current state/generation via currentState before checks.

questions: When a deferred callback (Allow's done or Execute's afterRequest) runs after a generation change, the outcome is silently dropped by afterRequest line 299; is this intended deferred-completion accounting behavior or a gap?

Counts doc says CircuitBreaker clears Counts on state change or at closed intervals, but beforeRequest increments counts.Requests (line 289) even in half-open before generation validity is re-checked; is that intended?

Execute's panic path calls afterRequest(generation, false) before re-panicking (line 237-238); should a panic count as a failure even if the request never returned an error, and is that resolved intent?

TwoStepCircuitBreaker.Allow returns a done callback the caller may invoke later or never; there is no source-specified requirement that done be called exactly once, nor any error returned for a late callback affected by generation mismatch — is that unresolved?

onStateChange is invoked inside setState while the mutex is held (line 359); source does not specify whether the callback may safely call back into the breaker (e.g., State or Counts) — is reentrancy supported or unspecified?

currentState in closed state may call toNewGeneration (line 338) without changing state, clearing counts; does that mean interval expiry silently drops in-flight deferred outcomes via generation mismatch, and is that intended?

In open state, currentState transitions to half-open (line 342) and toNewGeneration clears counts and leaves expiry zero; source does not specify whether there is a cooldown or window limiting half-open attempts beyond maxRequests — is that a gap?

defaultReadyToTrip uses ConsecutiveFailures > 5 (line 193) while docs say 'more than 5' (line 98); consistent, but the ordering between counts.onFailure and readyToTrip invocation when multiple concurrent failures resolve is not specified beyond generation check — unresolved?

beforeRequest returns the captured generation even on ErrOpenState/ErrTooManyRequests (lines 284, 286); since Execute ignores generation on the error path (line 230-231), source does not state whether returned generation on rejection has any meaning — unspecified?

Settings.MaxRequests=0 is normalized to 1 (lines 147-148), and half-open rejection compares counts.Requests >= maxRequests (line 285); after a half-open success closes the breaker then reopens, source does not specify how many half-open probes occur across the open->half-open transition — unresolved?
